hot.title: Evolving Agent Teams
hot.summary: Evolving Agent Teams changes how coding agents are organized during GPU kernel optimization. A supervisor diagnoses stalled progress, redesigns roles and coordination, and preserves lessons and code in a shared filesystem. On DeepSeek-V3 MLA paged decode, additional-budget runs achieve 1.21× geometric-mean speedup over production FlashInfer across 47 H100 workloads, with 36 faster; 11 remain slower, without beating the run-stage-only reference.

hot.title: How to Train a One-Step Language Model Without a Teacher
hot.summary: Discrete Beckmann Transport Models (DBTM) learn a time-independent endpoint map from data by minimizing a conservation-equation self-regression objective, with no teacher model or time conditioning. At inference, each map application proposes a complete sequence, and additional function evaluations use commit-and-renoise refinement rather than ODE integration. DBTM reports coherence–diversity Pare

hot.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
hot.summary: ThinkWorld addresses robot-learning by grounding robot actions and annotated human hand motion in a shared discrete Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD) vocabulary. It trains on action-unlabeled videos by rewarding tokens whose predicted futures match observed futures. At deployment, a separate expert predicts continuous actions. In real-robot trials, it achieved 94.4% macro success across six task-condition combinations and succeeded in 52/60 OOD trials.

hot.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
hot.summary: GEPA-Curator improves prompt optimization by selecting task experiences for learning and retrieving a prior success when a task fails. It maintains task histories, skips tasks unlikely to provide useful signal, and gives the optimizer a same-task reference when available. In experiments, it scores 88.6% on GitLab validation; gains vary by setting and do not establish that every failure is noisy.

hot.title: Timestral
hot.summary: Timestral is a time-series forecasting model that learns across series and forecasts new ones without retraining. It keeps observed history available while adding separate prediction positions, and assigns covariates roles so known-future inputs can be used without exposing future targets. Timestral-209M ranks first among compared models on six metrics across three benchmarks; this does not isolate DHF’s contribution.

hot.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
hot.summary: FLORE connects force-annotated demonstrations to force-aware control for humanoid contact tasks. Its diffusion policy uses wrist images, robot state, and hand wrenches to predict motion and per-hand force commands, which a controller tracks. On Unitree G1, FLORE succeeds in 24 of 30 rollouts across three tasks, versus 8 of 30 for a position-only policy; evidence is limited to those tasks.

hot.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
hot.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio, and video into an embedding space for retrieval. Modality encoders turn media into tokens that a transformer pools into a vector; modular configurations omit encoders not needed. On MSEB(Retrieval), native audio scores 69.54 MRR@10 versus 57.59 for ASR/text, but uses more parameters. An intermediate MMEB-v2 ablation improves image and video scores, while visual-document performance remains nearly unchanged.

hot.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: CARD transfers human hand motion and contact intent to robot hands by encoding touch location, push direction, and force on semantic hand regions, then optimizing joint targets to align robot pads with those contacts. On 20 monocular-video clips retargeted to SHARPA Wave, CARD established contact on 61.4% of anchor-frames, versus 9.7% for DexPilot; this is geometric fidelity, not task success.

hot.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
hot.summary: FVQ represents visual features as multiple discrete codes for multimodal understanding, using complementary views quantized independently. In a shared QwenViT setting, its eight-benchmark average rises from 63.9 at 112 bits per patch to 65.3 at 224 bits, while RVQ stays at 64.0. The industrial-scale model improves over UniAR and Emu3-Chat, but trails continuous Qwen3-VL on the nine-metric average.

hot.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
hot.summary: The authors introduce a two-stage text-to-image system: an autoregressive (AR) model predicts visual tokens from a prompt, then diffusion renders pixels from them. They freeze the pretrained AR backbone while training the renderer. A roughly 3-billion-parameter model trained with 6,600 H100 GPU-hours scores 0.86 on GenEval and 87.78 on DPG-Bench, supporting this recipe but not universal superiority or optimal compute allocation.

hot.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
hot.summary: The authors propose a framework for understanding work agents as systems accountable for verified outcomes rather than models producing answers or tool calls. It combines a model, harness, and workspace, and distinguishes persistence—when responsibility can close—from openness—what must be discovered. The survey synthesizes five work forms and capability families but does not establish improved performance or reliability.

hot.title: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception
hot.summary: ActiveAlign links camera calibration and tactile feedback for robot manipulation. ActiveAlign-Waving uses multiple depth observations to calibrate the camera, while ActiveAlign-Touching builds a local tactile height map to guide contact. On a Unitree G1, the combined system achieved 14/20 Midi Slider successes, versus 3/20 for keypoint planning; the result is limited to demonstrated tasks, not arbitrary robots or objects.

hot.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
hot.summary: PDRVLA trains compact physical tokens to guide robot actions using predicted future scene features and auxiliary supervision from a frozen video world model. At deployment, it generates actions without running the video model. On LIBERO-Plus, it reaches 89.9% success, versus 89.0% for Qwen-RobotManip. A held-out prediction test shows lower mean normalized prediction MSE, but does not establish an action-success benefit. Benchmarks are simulated, and no control-latency measurement is reported.

hot.title: SpeeDiff: Scalable Pixel-Anchored End-to-End Latent Diffusion Model
hot.summary: SpeeDiff jointly trains an image encoder and diffusion generator, adding Tweedie Pixel Reconstruction (TPR) to decode the generator’s clean-latent estimate and compare it with the input pixels. On class-conditioned ImageNet 256×256 without guidance, TPR lowers gFID from 33.95 to 5.79 after 80 epochs. The result supports the pixel anchor in this setup, not attribution of later gains to TPR alone.

hot.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
hot.summary: SynthAPI lets researchers test how tool, task, and database-state diversity affect training for agents that use stateful tools. It varies apps, tasks per app, starting database profiles, and distractor data across training budgets. On held-out high-compute runs, its composition-aware scaling law reaches a 0.0285 MAE, versus 0.1706 for task count alone, with extrapolation up to 16×; validation covers one synthesis pipeline.

hot.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
hot.summary: The authors introduce executable code captions for structured 2D videos, encoding layout and time-dependent changes as rules that can be rendered into video. CodeCap-Bench evaluates the approach on 323 videos. In a tested question-answering setup, code-rendered videos scored 83.02%, versus 72.64% for natural-language captions; this is not a general guarantee, and models retained dynamic information less faithfully than static appearance and layout.

hot.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
hot.summary: EgoThumb uses a palm-facing camera and joint-position history to control a wearable thumb for hold-and-manipulate tasks. A learned policy selects thumb positions without a separate trigger motion. It averaged 0.90 success across four tasks for the demonstrator and at least 0.875 on two new users. Expanded object areas reduced success to 0.53 on Stir Tea and 0.17 on Transfer Ball.

hot.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
hot.summary: QCP lets users request execution quality by labeling successful trajectories with rule-based scores and conditioning a policy on those labels. It collects successful rollouts at the highest label, relabels data by measured quality, and retrains. On a conveyor, its highest-bin policy raises end-effector speed from 188.6 to 257.6 mm/s and throughput from 8.2 to 13.0 cans per minute versus BC.

hot.title: NyoomFloat12: Accelerating LLM Inference via Lossless 12-Bit Weight Compression
hot.summary: The authors introduce NF12, a lossless format that stores BF16 weights in 12 bits and reconstructs them in a GPU-friendly, fixed-length pattern. It exploits concentrated exponent values and handles rare exceptions separately. On a shared-prefix Qwen3-32B rollout workload, NF12 reaches a peak of 787 output tokens per second versus BF16’s 310, a schedule-dependent 2.54× ratio; gains are not universal.

hot.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
hot.summary: GPT-6-Astra directly controls robot manipulation in EBench and can also call post-trained policies to execute motion. The benchmark covers 510 simulated episodes across 26 tasks, using task success and partial stage completion. Direct control reaches 46.7% success; the InternW0-∆ harness reaches 56.0%, above the strongest standalone policy, but high-precision performance remains weak and handoffs can regress.

likes.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
likes.summary: The authors rewrite softmax cross-entropy and distillation calculations to preserve small gradient differences that standard arithmetic can round away. In reported modular-arithmetic experiments, the fixed loss prevents slingshot spikes and keeps an identical student and teacher at KL = 0. On one fp32 task, accuracy reaches 85% rather than falling to 23%; these extreme regimes are uncommon in large-scale training.

likes.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Tech Blog: Advancing Open Intelligence
likes.summary: Moonshot AI introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a post-trained version of Kimi K3 and its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a 1M-token context window and a 2-3× faster Highspeed variant. Trained with far more RL compute across hundreds of domains, it matches or approaches leading proprietary models on coding, 3D creation, finance, and agentic benchmarks. Moonshot also removed cyber-related training data on purpose, so the open weights stay behind the frontier on offensive cyber capability. Full weights are due by Nov 4, 2026.

likes.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False
likes.summary: The authors give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas with fixed-width clauses. It reorganizes assignment sums into group-by-group sums using shared measurements and interpolation. For each fixed width, the worst-case running time is polynomial in the input size times 2^{O(n log log n/√log n)}, with polynomial space; the exponent improves for linearly many clauses, but this does not give subexponential algorithms for general NP problems.

likes.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
likes.summary: LEAP learns a reusable cost to score trajectories from paths. It contrasts paths with samples from a reference process and combines a path log-ratio with the reference action. On a 31-body orbital benchmark, its model reaches 0.228 NRMSE versus about 1 for local models; molecular tests reuse the action for new requests. These results apply to the tested settings.

likes.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
likes.summary: The authors survey video world models through four relations to a world: reading its state, generating observations, sharing information between understanding and generation, and updating state under actions. They distinguish smooth frame-to-frame change from consistency across a world trajectory, and propose tests for state, control, and decision utility. The survey organizes research but reports no new experiment or performance gain.

likes.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
likes.summary: OPST trains models on self-generated questions from broad topic descriptions, without curated training questions or answers. A question-only student learns from token-level teacher guidance, while the teacher sees the generated candidate answer and rationale. On Gemma 4 E2B, MMLU rises from 37.5% to 47.7%, versus 38.3% for SFT and 37.3% for GRPO on the same data. Experiments use small models; verification checks consistency, not correctness.

likes.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
likes.summary: The authors introduce BeNice!, a fine-tuning method that trains looped language models to use the final recurrence’s key–value cache in earlier recurrences, reducing cache storage without removing recurrent computation. On a 770M model, shared-cache validation perplexity is 11.86 versus 21.61 after standard finetuning. Simulated serving shows 23.6% higher throughput at 2 requests per second; at low load, performance matches baseline.

likes.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
likes.summary: The authors compare persistent memory systems with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) from raw history, measuring query-level wins and losses against that reference. On LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.6-27B, SimpleMem reaches 73.6% judge accuracy, versus 81.4% for two-round RAG. Results vary across settings, so this comparison does not show that all memory systems underperform.

likes.title: Humanoid Mobility via Attention-based Contacts
likes.summary: The authors present a locomotion system that plans contacts rather than full-body motions. An attention-based planner selects terrain-aligned targets for nine body parts, while a controller turns them into movement; reference motions guide training but are not inputs at deployment. On eight simulation courses, it averages 92.5% success versus 58.8% for MGMT, limited to those courses.

likes.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
likes.summary: The Plan–Retrieve–Select workflow handles multi-part requests by splitting them into independent substeps, retrieving BM25 candidates, and having a trained model choose a tool for each. On 2,124 filtered ToolBench G3 test instructions, Qwen3-8B after SFT and RL achieves 41.5% exact-match success, versus 30.6% for prompted Llama-4-Maverick using a Search-R1-style protocol. This result is limited to tool selection on this benchmark.

likes.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
likes.summary: WeVisOne-VL integrates language-guided localization with instance-level masks and alpha mattes. It predicts coordinate tokens and follows each box with an <OBJ> marker, which connects the selected instance to a pixel decoder. On the in-house WeRefMat referring-prompt test, 4B records 9.8 MAD versus 22.4 for Qwen3.5-9B plus SAM2-Matting; this comparison does not establish broader superiority.

likes.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models For High Quality Image Synthesis
likes.summary: TEM lets a transformer-based energy-based model generate images by scoring samples in a pretrained autoencoder’s latent space and using Langevin sampling. Multiple energy heads and positive-only representation alignment support training, while adding energies enables the demonstrated concept composition without retraining. On class-conditional ImageNet, TEM-XL reports FID-50K 3.82 at 256×256 and 8.24 at 512×512, without classifier-free guidance.

likes.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
likes.summary: PhysLadder evaluates GPT-6 Astra on 16 household tasks in simulation and reality, organized by increasing interaction demands. Each task receives three zero-shot trials per environment, and level means weight tasks equally. Real-world success averages 80.0% at L1, 47.6% at L2, and 0.0% at L3; simulation shows 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. No L3 task succeeds; results describe this model and setup.

likes.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
likes.summary: UniAction represents each action with semantic identity and video-space/time coordinates, then processes action and video tokens together through a pretrained video model with calibrated attention. It is tested on force, camera, hand-pose, and robot-pose control using four datasets. On force Action Following, it scores 0.7630 versus 0.5436 for a force-specific expert, in this tested setup.

likes.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
likes.summary: The authors introduce S², an offline measure of whether a model’s sensory features reflect robot-motion geometry. It compares nearest neighbors across demonstrations in sensory and trajectory spaces, using cosine distance and dynamic time warping, then computes a centered, normalized CKNNA score. Across 12 fine-tuned VLAs, S² correlated with SimplerEnv success (r = +0.717), but does not establish causation or replace rollouts.

likes.title: Native Real-Time Interactive Omni Intelligence: A Unified Framework
likes.summary: The authors present a survey and framework for assistants that understand and respond while inputs and interaction states keep changing, rather than only after a finished prompt. They distinguish broad multimodal ability from using it in ongoing interaction, and describe streaming models and foreground–background coordination. The survey maps evidence but establishes neither a winning architecture nor that interactivity requires capability loss.

likes.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
likes.summary: The authors fit a cost-aware scaling law to choose the share of training tokens made up of rewrites in FineWeb-Edu experiments. They charge for target training and rewrite generation. At 10^22 FLOPs, the law selects 0.32; a 21.9B-parameter model scores 0.983 Paloma macro BPB versus 1.061 for natural-only training. This run is within 1.1% of forecast, in the tested setting.
